description:
A wrapped mark a scan found but could not read.

The text matched the scheme's `embeddedMarking` pattern, which is how a part marking is written, but recognition read no marking in it, and it has no entry in `ScanOutcome.results`. Text that looks like a marking and carries none is reported rather than dropped, so a reader can see it and correct it. `start`/`end` are offsets in UTF-16 code units in the input text, as on `ScanResult`.

end.description: End position in the input text

inner.description: The text inside the wrapper: the capture group of the scheme's `embeddedMarking` pattern.

leading.description: Whether the mark leads its line. The line starts at the beginning of the text or just after the last line feed before `start`, and the mark leads it when only whitespace lies between that point and `start`. Another mark is not whitespace, whether it was read or not: in `(S)(QQ)` and in `(S) (QQ)`, `(S)` leads its line and `(QQ)` does not.

start.description: Start position in the input text

text.description: The wrapped text as found in the document, wrapper included.
